newsitem.title: INDIA: Long wait for Reliance bonus nears end.
newsitem.headline: Long wait for Reliance bonus nears end.

text.p: Leading Indian private firm Reliance Industries cheered stock markets on Thursday when it said its board of directors would meet to discuss a bonus issue of shares later this month.
"The firm will be meeting for a bonus on June 26," a Reliance spokesman told Reuters on Thursday.
The announcement came nearly a year after chairman Dhirubhai Ambani hinted that shareholders were likely to receive a bonus issue in the coming months.
Reliance shares surged 18.50 rupees, or nearly six percent, to 339.50 in hectic trade on the Bombay bourse after the announcement.

"I guess it doesn't surprise me that they would do something like this. In a market like India a bonus issue is important and it results in a tremendous boost in sentiment," said a Hong Kong-based analyst with a U.S. brokerage.

The Reliance spokesman said the firm would meet to finalise a bonus issue of shares on June 26 -- the same day that Reliance is due to hold its annual shareholders meeting. Details of the timing of the meeting were not immediately available.
Reliance has issued two bonus share issues since it was listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on January 23, 1978.
Both times the firm gave investors three bonus shares for every five held and early speculation in the stock markets was that the company was likely to maintain this ratio.

Rumours of a bonus share issue in Reliance have bubbled since the firm's last shareholder meeting in July when Ambani told shareholders -- who asked him about a bonus issue -- they would not be disappointed at the next annual meeting.
"It's been a while since these rumours had been floating and people had sort of given up," said Sanjay Vaid, chief dealer at Lloyds Securities.
"The news has definitely changed the market sentiment."
The company's shares have risen around 60 percent this year on the back of large capacity additions, increased profits and hopes of a bonus share issue.
Some petrochemicals analysts said the announcement had taken them by surprise.
"I'm surprised. I was not expecting a bonus," said an analyst at a foreign broking firm. "I didn't think they would do it. They have given very few bonus issues in the past."

"It shows the management's confidence in how they see the prospects of the company in the coming years. It also shows that Ambani wanted to keep his shareholders happy -- he has kept his promise," the analyst said.
